title: Deteriorated House: When to Strengthen or Repair, and When to Rebuild?
desc: Repair or rebuild a deteriorating old house? How to assess its condition, criteria to compare cost and risk, and rules for houses showing signs of danger.
summary: How to assess an old house, the criteria for deciding between strengthening, repair or rebuilding, and the rules on maintenance and handling houses showing signs of danger.
body: p

Houses 20–30 years old usually start to leak, crack and see their electrical and plumbing deteriorate. The homeowner's biggest question is: keep repairing, or demolish and rebuild? There is no universal answer – it must be based on an assessment of the existing condition and a sober comparison of cost and benefit.
h2
1. The first step: assess the existing condition
p

Before deciding, have an engineer survey: the load-bearing structure (foundation, columns, beams, slabs), the degree of settlement or tilting, leakage, steel corrosion, the electrical and plumbing systems and the roof. If the old drawings are no longer available, a measured survey of the existing condition may be needed. The Construction Law also sets the principle that the owner is responsible for maintaining the building during use (Article 65 of the Construction Law 2025).
h2
2. When are repair and strengthening reasonable?
ul
The load-bearing structure is basically still sound; damage is mainly in finishes (plastering, paint, tiles, waterproofing, electrical and plumbing).
The layout and function of the house still suit the family's needs.
Localized structural damage, with a clear strengthening solution (jacketing columns, reinforcing beams, treating rusted reinforcement, etc.).
Legal or planning constraints make it hard for a new building to reach the existing size.
h2
3. When should rebuilding be considered?
ul
The foundation has settled and tilted severely, and strengthening it is costly and risky.
Structural deterioration is widespread, with crumbling concrete and rusted steel in many places.
An old load-bearing brick-wall house, where a major change of layout is needed or floors are to be added.
The estimated repair cost is already close to the cost of new construction while the remaining service life is not commensurate.
p

When comparing, do not look only at the total sum: account for the time of renting temporary housing, permits, the risk of extra costs when opening up the structure (repairing an old house usually brings more extras than expected), and the number of additional years of use under each option. See also what a construction cost estimate includes.
h2
4. A house showing signs of danger: no delay
p

Under Article 42 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP, when a building is at risk of being unsafe, the owner must inspect its condition, have its quality assessed if necessary, apply emergency measures (limit or stop use, cordon off the area, move people and property), report to the local authority, and repair or demolish when needed. A competent state agency that discovers a dangerous building also has the right to require the owner to survey, assess, repair or demolish it.
p

For a building past its design service life, Article 43 requires assessment, strengthening and reporting to the state agency if it is to continue in use – but except for detached houses of households and individuals. Although this procedure is not compulsory, an old house should still be assessed periodically for the safety of the family itself.
h2
5. Procedures for repair or rebuilding
ul
Interior repair that does not affect the load-bearing structure and does not change the use: usually exempt from a permit under Point h, Clause 2, Article 43 of the Construction Law 2025.

Renovation that affects the structure, or an exterior adjoining an urban street subject to architectural management requirements: a repair and renovation permit is needed (file under Article 61 of Decree 217/2026/ND-CP).
Demolishing and rebuilding: follow the procedure for new construction – see procedure for a detached house construction permit.
p

note

This article is for reference; the decision to strengthen or rebuild must be based on a survey and assessment by a qualified person. Regulations are cited under Construction Law 135/2025/QH15, Decree 207/2026/ND-CP and 217/2026/ND-CP (in force).
